assessments.reasoning: The project-controlled GitHub wiki lists the full Home revision in its page history. Its revision-addressed rendering contains the same opening deprecation notice and dialect-and-target statement as the freshly acquired raw Home. The raw source matches the registered SHA-256, its cited four-line slice digest and the disclosed Git blob ID. The sentence attributes the source dialect to Clojure and treats JavaScript as the deployment platform.

The exact site README belongs to the project-owned documentation repository and names ClojureScript as a programming language. Its first seven lines and complete bytes match the supplied witnesses, and the GitHub blob at the original lead's pinned commit embeds the same raw lines. The README does not cover the historical wiki statement, the parent dialect relation, or the deployment target. It provides relevant name and project-scope context.

challenge.method: Reacquire the exact registered raw documents, recompute their four- and seven-line witness digests, and verify the wiki project's link to its pinned revision and historical rendered content. Compare the current official ClojureScript homepage, Differences from Clojure, Rationale and compiler repository description. Check competing readings of ClojureScript as only a compiler, an alternate name for JVM Clojure, JavaScript itself, or Google Closure.
challenge.results: The pinned wiki prose names the Clojure-derived source dialect and JavaScript deployment. The currently maintained homepage separately calls ClojureScript a language and describes the project's compiler, and the differences and rationale pages preserve the source and target distinction. The language's project name is shared by the compiler. The site documentation and wiki have the same project lineage. The old wiki remains suitable for the dated-by-revision attribution, while the deprecation notice limits current authority.

limitations: The deprecation notice redirects project documentation work to the site. This review supports the exact archived descriptive identity statement.

The registered raw wiki route is mutable. This review also checked the historic revision link and recomputed the captured Git blob ID and citation span. The full wiki repository HEAD was different from the identified historical page revision.
The proposed dialect identity leaves tool identity, supported runtime versions, interoperability and source compatibility to separate claims. Active is an index classification.
The site README supplies context and shares project lineage with the support source. It is insufficient as support for the parent and deployment-target proposition.
Revision 1 remains held. The review conclusion applies to revision 2 and the exact bindings reviewed here.
